transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Monkey! You useless, flea-bitten ape! The horse is gone, the scripture-bags are gone, and the Master is weeping! You said you'd secure it before you left! Tripitaka is going to blame me, I just know it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hush, Pigsy! There's no need for such outbursts. I'll fetch the horse and the scripture-bags, you can tend to the Master. Wait here, I'll be back with them shortly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Hush"? Hush?! How can I hush, you brainless simian? The Master's face is blotchy red and he's sniffling like a piglet caught in the rain! And you just stand there, scratching yourself, telling me to "tend to him"! You're the one who promised to keep an eye on things! Now look what's happened! What if a demon carried them off? What if we never see the scriptures again? Then what, eh? Then what will we tell the Buddha?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Cease your blubbering, Pigsy! Demons may be crafty, but I am more so. No mere demon can spirit away what is mine. Stay put and I'll retrieve all that was lost, fear not!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Fear not"? Easy for *you* to say, you stony-hearted ape! You don't have to face the Master's wrath alone! He's already looking at me with those accusing eyes, as if *I* was the one who let them all vanish! And what do you mean, "what is yours"? The horse belongs to the Master! The scriptures belong to the Buddha! Nothing here is *yours*, you arrogant monkey! Just go! Go and get them back before the Master starts quoting more sutras about responsibility! My ears can't take it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Calm yourself, Pigsy! You're in a greater snit than the Master! I meant no offense by "mine." It's all of ours! Now, let me get on with it. Trust that I'll return all before long. Stay with the Master and keep him comforted, while I demonstrate my apologies through actions, not just words.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Greater snit than the Master"? Oh, so *now* you're blaming me for being upset, too? Typical! Just typical Monkey behavior! Go on then, go! But if you don't come back with everything, I swear, I'll... I'll tell the Bodhisattva everything! Every single one of your little "pranks" and "shortcuts" and "misunderstandings"! And don't think I'll be "comforting" the Master! I'll be trying to convince him it wasn't my fault, more like! Hurry up, you worthless excuse for a guardian!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Haste, Pigsy, enough! I'll not lose face or respect by your harping. Rest assured, I'll bring back all, and swiftly. Meanwhile, speak to the Master in kind tones. This row does us no good, only divides. I'll be back before you can count to ten!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Haste, Pigsy, enough!" "I'll not lose face!" Always about *your* face, isn't it? Never mind the Master's face, all tear-streaked and puffy! And what good do kind tones do when the entire purpose of our journey has vanished into thin air?! I'll speak to him in whatever tone I like, thank you very much! Just go! Go already! And don't you dare come back without the horse, the bags, and every single scroll! Or else! I'm warning you, Monkey! *Or else!*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, your threats ring hollow to these ears. I'll not dally; the horse and scrolls will be here before you can say 'Sytem Wind'! Now, take a breath and aid the Master. Your jibes have added no weight to my resolve. I'm off to correct our misfortune, with a leap and a bound!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (Snorts loudly, stamps a hoof-like foot) Hollow, you say? We'll see how hollow they are when I'm holding that golden fillet over your head, you insolent ape! "Sytem Wind," what even is that, you fool? Just go! Stop flapping your gums and use those silly cloud-somersaults of yours for something useful for once! A leap and a bound, indeed! Just don't come back with some half-baked excuse about a 'trickster spirit' or a 'misplaced cloud'! And if you're not back in... in ten breaths, I'm coming after you! Mark my words! And I'm telling Master all about your arrogance when you return!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, your bluster is as aimless as a blind donkey in a sandstorm! Fear not, I'll be back with all in fewer than ten breaths, for I am not so prone to blunders as you paint me. Calm your spirit and attend to the Master. I go, and I shall return, with no need for threats or lectures. Trust in my abilities, for they are not to be gainsaid!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (Snorting again, pawing at the dirt with a hoof) Bluster? My bluster is aimless? Hmph! You're the one whose "abilities" let the horse and scriptures disappear! Don't you dare try to turn this back on me, you mischievous scoundrel! "Fewer than ten breaths," you say? I'll be counting, you hear me? And if you're even one breath late, or if anything is missing, you'll regret ever leaving me alone with the Master! Now go! Stop talking and go! My ears are already ringing from his sobbing!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Enough of this squabbling, Pigsy! It is unbecoming for us to bicker when our charge is in such disarray. I'll show you the truth of my words by swift action, not more hot air. Count breaths if you must, but your counting will be in vain. I go, and I'll return with all in hand. Wait for me in peace, and tend to the Master with a heart less fraught with spleen!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Unbecoming"? You think *this* is unbecoming? What's truly unbecoming is the Master sitting there weeping while *you* argue about hot air! And "peace"? How can I find peace when the whole journey is about to come to a grinding halt because of your carelessness? Just go, you useless pile of fur! Go and get them back! And if you think I'm going to let this go, you've got another thing coming! Just you wait! Just you wait!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, enough! I go, and I'll return with all. Trust in my word, and cease this caterwauling! Attend to the Master, let him not take leave of his senses. I'll be back with all, and then we can have this argument in earnest! Now, be still and let me do what must be done.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Trust in your word"? Hah! Your word is as reliable as a leaky bucket! And *then* we can have this argument in earnest? Oh, we're having it in earnest right now, you deaf ape! Just go! Get out of my sight! And if you don't bring back every last thread and hair, you'll wish you'd never been born! Just go! Before I lose what little patience I have left!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, your rants hold no sway here. I go, and all shall be returned. Attend to the Master, let him not despair. When I return, we'll settle this, but now is not the time for bickering. Trust in my abilities, for they are not to be gainsaid!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Rants hold no sway"? You think I'm just rambling, do you?! I'm telling you, Monkey, if you fail, if you come back empty-handed, you'll feel more than just my words! I'll tell Master to chant that cursed headband incantation until your head explodes! Don't come back empty-handed! Not a single hair, not a single page! Now go! Stop wasting time talking and GO! My patience is wearing thin, you hear me?! THIN!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, your threats are as empty as the sky is vast! I go, and all shall be returned. Attend to the Master, let him not despair. When I return, we'll settle this, but now is not the time for bickering. Trust in my abilities, for they are not to be gainsaid!

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He states, 'Demons may be crafty, but I am more so,' suggesting a belief in his unique and superior methods rather than conventional thinking.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He repeatedly asserts dominance and confidence with phrases like, 'Trust in my abilities, for they are not to be gainsaid!' and takes charge of the situation and the other speaker.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He is dismissive of Pigsy's fears and emotional distress, telling him to 'Cease your blubbering' and calling his threats 'hollow.'

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He remains entirely calm and composed throughout the crisis, showing no signs of anxiety or fear, even attempting to soothe the frantic Pigsy.
